verdict.rationale: Yubico's own PGP docs say the YubiKey runs OpenPGP sign and encrypt operations with a private key stored on the device. Community users confirm it works as a GPG/OpenPGP smart card (e.g. with pass). The pack never documents git commit signing or encrypted-email workflows themselves, so those use cases are only implied by generic OpenPGP sign/encrypt support. missing for 10: documented git commit-signing setup, documented encrypted-email (e.g. GPG mail client) workflow, independent hands-on corroboration of those use cases.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep OpenPGP keys on the device and use them for git commit signing and encrypted email

citations.quote: OpenPGP is an open standard for signing and encrypting. It enables RSA or ECC sign/encrypt operations using a private key stored on a smartcard (such as YubiKeys)
Yubikeys are the only ones I've found that support both FIDO2/WebAuthn as well as GPG smart card functionality for use with pass(1).
